title: Sharp cocone simplicial sets: vertex isofibration and join associativity
statement:
Use the small simplicial sets, quasicategories, equivalence edges and functor simplicial sets of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and isofibrations as defined in [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], in any fixed sufficiently large universes. For simplicial sets $A,B$, define their sharp join by
$$(A\star B)_n=A_n\amalg B_n\amalg\coprod_{a+b+1=n}A_a\times B_b,$$
with simplicial operators restricting the ordered block of $A$-vertices followed by the block of $B$-vertices; an empty block is the corresponding pure simplex. In particular $A^{\triangleright}=A\star\Delta^0$.
Let $p:K\to\mathcal C$ be a map from a small simplicial set to a quasicategory. Define the sharp cocone simplicial set $S_p(\mathcal C)$ by
$$S_p(\mathcal C)_n=\{u:K\star\Delta^n\to\mathcal C\mid u|_K=p\},$$
with operators induced by $\operatorname{id}_K\star\Delta(\alpha)$, and its vertex projection $S_p(\mathcal C)\to\mathcal C$ by restriction to $\Delta^n$. Then $S_p(\mathcal C)$ is a quasicategory and the vertex projection is an isofibration: it has the right lifting property against every inner horn inclusion $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $0<i<n$, and for every vertex $u$ of $S_p(\mathcal C)$ with vertex $x$, every equivalence edge $e:x\to y$ of $\mathcal C$ lifts to an equivalence edge of $S_p(\mathcal C)$ with source $u$ and image $e$.
For every small simplicial set $L$, maps $r:L\to S_p(\mathcal C)$ correspond bijectively to maps $t:K\star L\to\mathcal C$ with $t|_K=p$, naturally in $L$. Under this correspondence, associativity of the ordered joins, $(K\star L)\star\Delta^n=K\star(L\star\Delta^n)$, gives a simplicial isomorphism
$$S_r(S_p(\mathcal C))\cong S_t(\mathcal C).$$
The correspondence and this isomorphism preserve vertex projections and are natural in functors $\mathcal C\to\mathcal C'$ of quasicategories and in restriction along maps of the indexing simplicial sets $K$ and $L$. No filteredness, nonemptiness or colimit-existence hypothesis is imposed on $K$, $L$ or $\mathcal C$; the cases $K=\varnothing$ (then $S_p(\mathcal C)=\mathcal C$) and $L=\varnothing$ are included.
